findings.title: Compassion-name as agent
findings.claim: The definite compassion-name is the singular agent that performs the future act for the beneficiaries and places affection as its object.
findings.mechanism: The nominative name is delayed until after the beneficiary phrase, then governs the making verb; the following affection noun completes the agent-beneficiary-object relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The promise has a named compassionate agent, not an impersonal change in social feeling.
findings.containment: The grammar identifies the agent but does not by itself specify the human response or make the recipients the direct object.

epistemic.reason: The local morphology and supplied support directly ground the stated relation.

findings.title: Mercy-name meets affection
findings.claim: The mercy and tenderness field of al-Raḥmān colors the agent who places wuddan for the group.
findings.mechanism: The compassion-name as carrier meets the affection noun as an independent object; their contact makes the promise an act of compassionate agency rather than an abstract social result.
findings.reader_payoff: The affection promised is locally connected to the named agent's mercy field.
findings.containment: Kinship and womb associations remain root-family pressure, not a separate image activated by this focus wording.

epistemic.reason: The form and root support the mercy-affection contact, while adjacent root-family associations are not locally triggered.

findings.title: Mercy becomes the agent of affection
findings.claim: The local sequence lets the mercy-name explain the source of the affection that is placed for the beneficiaries.
findings.mechanism: The beneficiary phrase arrives before the delayed nominative agent, and wuddan follows as the object; mercy therefore meets a concrete relational outcome in the same ayah.
findings.reader_payoff: The divine compassion-name stands between the recipients and the affection result as the agent of the promised act.
findings.containment: This preserves the local contact only; it does not import the wider mercy-thread comparisons named by the source support.

epistemic.reason: The focus syntax is direct evidence; interpreting the named agent and affection object as a local mercy-to-love movement is a bounded synthesis.

findings.title: Indefinite affection object
findings.claim: Wuddan is an indefinite accusative gerund functioning as the direct object of the future making verb.
findings.mechanism: The object slot is filled by an open, indefinite affection noun rather than by a specified token of love, so the promise names affection qualitatively.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees affection itself as the promised result, with its instance left open.
findings.containment: The indefinite form does not claim that affection has no concrete recipients; li-hum supplies them.

epistemic.reason: QAC and attachment evidence directly identify the indefinite accusative object.

findings.title: Steady relational affection
findings.claim: The final noun carries steady loving attachment and communal warmth within the local affection branch.
findings.mechanism: The form and its supplied root analysis meet the beneficiary phrase and future placement frame; that contact keeps affection relationally directed while variant vowels leave the object as affection.
findings.reader_payoff: The outcome can be heard as durable closeness, not merely an unnamed emotional impulse.
findings.containment: Variants and more distant place-name, idol-name, peg, and wishing branches remain counter-readings rather than the focus reading.

epistemic.reason: The word analysis selects affection locally and explicitly preserves variant and neighboring-branch pressure.

findings.title: Promise lands on affection
findings.claim: The future making clause ends on wuddan, leaving affection as the last stated result of the promise.
findings.mechanism: The recipient phrase and named agent lead into the direct-object noun; its final position makes the promised relation the clause's landing point.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence closes on what the group receives: affection.
findings.containment: This is a focus-local endpoint reading; solitude and affection-root comparisons from other ayat are excluded.

epistemic.reason: The final object position is local evidence; the broader answer-to-aloneness reading is not retained.

findings.title: Assertion governs the promise
findings.claim: Inna places the relative class and the later future act inside one asserted frame.
findings.mechanism: The particle governs alladhina; the completed qualification clause then leads to the future making predicate, so assertion scopes the whole promise.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the affection promise as declared news rather than an unframed possibility.
findings.containment: The future event remains future; assertion does not supply a timetable or describe how affection appears.

epistemic.reason: The particle's governance and scope are supplied by QAC and attachment evidence.

findings.title: Emphasis over the qualifying class
findings.claim: The doubled emphatic particle reinforces the promise while the relative clause identifies the class it concerns.
findings.mechanism: Inna meets the following plural relative subject and its qualifications, giving the later future predicate settled declarative force without changing its future aspect.
findings.reader_payoff: The class is treated as established, and its promised affection as affirmed.
findings.containment: Emphasis does not turn the qualifying class into a closed lineage or erase the future form.

epistemic.reason: The particle's emphatic force is supplied, while its discourse payoff is an interpretation of the local scope.

findings.title: Relative pronoun opens the subject class

epistemic.reason: QAC and attachment evidence directly ground the governed relative construction.

findings.title: Membership defined by acts

findings.mechanism: Alladhina introduces a plural class; āmanū and ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāti supply its qualifying content.

findings.reader_payoff: Belief is presented as an established qualification of the group.
findings.containment: The perfect form marks the clause's act; it does not alone make a claim about the group's entire life history.

findings.title: Action hinges belief to its deed-object

findings.title: Definite category of sound deeds
findings.claim: The definite plural active participle al-ṣāliḥāti is the object performed and presents sound deeds as a recognized category.

findings.containment: The form does not specify an exhaustive list of which acts belong to that category.

epistemic.reason: QAC and attachment evidence directly identify the definite plural object.

findings.title: Soundness and repair color the deeds
findings.claim: The ṣāliḥāt category carries soundness, rightness, repair, and fitness pressure into the performed deeds.
findings.mechanism: The active-participle noun is the object of intentional action; that contact makes repair or soundness a quality of acts rather than a separate proper name or place.
findings.reader_payoff: Good deeds become perceptible as acts with a sound-making or reparative quality.
findings.containment: The root pressure remains within the locally selected ethical-deed category; it does not make every use of the root a repair act.

epistemic.reason: The supplied root range supports soundness and repair, with the local plural object bounding its application.

findings.title: The qualification lands before the promise
findings.claim: The relative subject clause closes on its deed-object before the future making predicate begins.
findings.mechanism: The sequence completes the group description with al-ṣāliḥāti and only then opens sa-yajʿalu; the clause boundary lets the ethical profile land before the affection promise.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader first receives the qualified group, then the act promised for them.
findings.containment: This is a local order-and-boundary observation; formula parallels named by the support are excluded.

findings.title: Assured future making
findings.claim: Sa-yajʿalu frames the placement of affection as a future act held in assurance.
findings.mechanism: The future prefix and imperfect verb meet the beneficiary phrase and direct-object affection noun, making the act future-facing while specifying its recipients and result.
findings.reader_payoff: The promise has a stated future orientation and a defined result for a beneficiary group.
findings.containment: The future marker does not give a date or define the means by which affection appears.

epistemic.reason: The future-marked imperfect and its attachment are directly supported by QAC and verb-instance evidence.

findings.title: Affection placed for recipients
findings.claim: Yajʿalu is locally read as placing or configuring affection for the beneficiaries.
findings.mechanism: The making verb meets li-hum as recipient relation and wuddan as its object; this complements frame selects relational placement rather than bare creation.
findings.reader_payoff: The promise pictures affection as a relation arranged for the group.
findings.containment: This is not a claim of creation from nothing or of an unrelated making branch.

epistemic.reason: The local recipient and object narrow the broad making field to relational placement.

findings.title: Preposition routes the promise to beneficiaries
findings.claim: The bound li preposition marks the group as beneficiaries for whom affection is placed.
findings.mechanism: Li governs the attached pronoun and contrasts with the direct-object slot later filled by wuddan; the contact prevents the group from being misread as the thing made.
findings.reader_payoff: The promise is routed toward its recipients, while affection remains the object.
findings.containment: The beneficiary relation does not specify a direct human act of reciprocation.

epistemic.reason: The prepositional attachment and direct-object contrast are directly supplied.

findings.title: Benefit and direction in li-hum
findings.claim: The preposition gives the affection placement a direction toward the group and marks their beneficiary relation.
findings.mechanism: The bound li and plural pronoun meet the affection object; their relation places love on the recipients' side of the promise.
findings.reader_payoff: The promised affection is directed for them rather than naming them as an object made.
findings.containment: The construction marks benefit and direction without specifying who among others expresses the affection.

epistemic.reason: The local recipient phrase supports this relational coloring of the preposition.

findings.title: Recipients precede the named giver
findings.claim: The promise presents its beneficiaries before naming the divine agent who acts for them.
findings.mechanism: The li-hum phrase precedes al-Raḥmān in the local order; the recipients are encountered first, then the agent and affection object complete the promise.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence lets the promise land on the qualified group before naming its giver.
findings.containment: This is a local ordering payoff, not a claim that the agent is absent or grammatically delayed beyond the supplied order.

epistemic.reason: The word order and beneficiary phrase are supplied; the foregrounding effect is bounded to that order.

findings.title: Plural pronoun in beneficiary slot
findings.claim: The attached plural pronoun carries the previously defined group into the beneficiary phrase under the preposition.
findings.mechanism: The relative class is followed by its qualification clause, and the governed pronoun returns that same class as recipients; it does not create a new subject.
findings.reader_payoff: The group moves from being described to being addressed as beneficiaries without repetition.
findings.containment: The local grammar supplies the antecedent relation; no cross-ayah narrowing is included.

epistemic.reason: QAC and attachment evidence directly identify the governed prepositional pronoun.

findings.title: The suffix carries the class forward
findings.claim: The plural suffix compactly carries the relative-clause group into the beneficiary slot.
findings.mechanism: The attached pronoun points back to the defined group without restating the belief-and-deed phrase; the repeated reference now marks recipients.
findings.reader_payoff: The long subject description can be heard once, then carried into the promise by a compact pronoun.
findings.containment: The candidate's separate 19:95 narrowing claim is not included here.

epistemic.reason: The supplied lexical support directly identifies the attached suffix's carried antecedent.

findings.title: Secure assent becomes reparative practice and affection
findings.claim: Where a general promise says that believers who do good receive love, this focus sequence can also be read as assent entering intentional repair, with the Compassionate rendering that practice into an affection-shaped social state.
findings.mechanism: The assent carrier at āmanū meets the independent action and righteous-deed clause; soundness gives that practice a reparative direction. The future making verb then contacts the beneficiary phrase and wuddan, while al-Raḥmān names the agent. The sequence moves from the baseline's general reward to a connected path from inward trust through practice into a conferred relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The class's qualification, the quality of its deeds, the named agent, and the affection result become one linked movement rather than unrelated labels.
findings.containment: This attributed synthesis extends the ordinary promise intact. Faith remains believing and trusting, ṣāliḥāt remains the righteous-deed category, and the claim does not guarantee a specific human response or announce a surah-wide system.

epistemic.reason: The focus QAC and word-analysis supports ground the local carriers and grammar; the six-part semantic chain comes from a legacy-unbound HFT nomination and is retained with attribution rather than treated as a settled lexical result.

findings.title: Reconciliatory dealings settle into affection
findings.claim: Where the baseline leaves righteous deeds as an undifferentiated class rewarded with favor, this focus can be read as interpersonal dealings whose reconciliatory content is made into a settled relation of affection.
findings.mechanism: The dealing carrier at ʿamilū meets ṣāliḥāt as reconciliation that removes aversion; yajʿalu gives that episodic repair a settled state, and wuddan names the resulting affection. The beneficiary pronoun and plural class make the path relational. Thus the baseline reward reading gains a specific attributed route from human repair to reciprocal closeness.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive good deeds as social repair whose yield is affection, not only as a general qualifying category.
findings.containment: The local ethical-deed reading remains intact. The HFT role is attributed and does not claim that every righteous deed is reconciliation or that reciprocity is grammatically guaranteed.

epistemic.reason: Local forms and recipient/object relations are supplied; the reconciliation sequence is a legacy-unbound contextual nomination evaluated against those focus carriers.

findings.title: Affection as exploratory recompense
findings.claim: As an exploratory analogy, the ayah can assign affection itself as a nonmonetary recompense for reparative work, where the baseline leaves love as one unspecified reward among others.
findings.mechanism: The work carrier at ʿamilū meets the future assignment frame at yajʿalu and the beneficiary phrase li-hum; wuddan fills the result slot. The work-wage and assigned-fee facets therefore open a compensation analogy, and affection occupies its outcome. This changes the unspecified-reward baseline into a possible work-to-recompense relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the promised affection as the result assigned to those who perform the deeds, not merely as another item in an unnamed reward set.
findings.containment: This is exploratory analogy. ʿAmilū remains an ethical-action verb, yajʿalu does not mean wage or fee, and wuddan remains affection rather than a legal payment or the only reward.

epistemic.reason: The local work, assignment, recipient, and object forms make the analogy possible, but its wage/fee chain comes from a legacy-unbound HFT trace expressly marked exploratory.

branch_activations.boundary: Yajʿalu does not lexically mean wage or fee here; this is an analogy, not a contractual payment or exclusive reward.
